Hi Laura — thanks for the sample. Quick read-through and some high-level framing below; Karthik and I can follow up with a one-page commercial and rough savings estimates tomorrow.

Short answers first:
- Packaging: Starter (no commit, pay-as-you-go + advisory) | Committed (3/12 month commit w/ credits & ops hours) | Enterprise (annual commit + prioritized Dedicated capacity + extended observability).
- Savings levers: continuous batching (low latency impact for small requests), prefix/KV caching (highest ROI when your calls are repetitive), and model quantization (best for long-form where slight quality delta is acceptable).

Tradeoff bullets:
- If ~70% of calls are <128 tokens, batching will reduce per-token overhead but only after adding small request coalescing; estimate 8–12% unit cost drop for starter, 15–25% with committed batch sizing optimizations.
- KV/prefix caching: if you have repeated prompts among the 70% small calls, caching can yield 20–40% token reduction on those requests depending on hit rate.
- Quantization: for your >512 token workloads, moving 16-bit -> 8-bit (q4/INT8) variants typically gives 30–50% cost reduction with <3% subjective quality delta in most summarization workloads; we recommend evaluating on a small eval set.

I've attached a pricing matrix and a blank workload workbook to capture expected hit rates and commit levels (Optimize_pricing_matrix_v1.xlsx - stub). Can you share a couple of representative prompts and an eval set for the >512 token flows?

Next steps: Karthik will add concretes on quant variants and latency implications; Lauren can draft the commercial one-pager for your finance team. If you prefer a quick call to walk through the matrix, we have availability Thu 7/16 11am PT.

Cheers,
Hannah Schmitt

Laura / Hannah — quick technical note on quant and latency tradeoffs based on AuroraScale's token distribution: 

- Recommendation: Pilot q4_8bit variant for long-form summarization first (samples >512). q4 gives good latency improvement on Ampere/RTX-class GPUs, and we have validated pipeline support for seamless fallback to fp16 when quality regresses.
- Metrics to track during pilot: per-token latency (p50/p95), ROUGE/BERTScore delta on eval set, KV cache hit rate, and end-to-end tail latency with batching enabled.
- Batching config: use adaptive micro-batch sizing with a 15ms aggregation window for your <128 token tier to preserve low p50 while improving throughput. We expect a small p95 uplift (~10–20ms) unless your requests are extremely latency-sensitive.

Commercial tradeoffs (short):
- If AuroraScale can commit 6–12 months of expected tokens at a 20–30% baseline reduction target, we can layer a commit discount (starts at 12% for 6-month, 18% for 12-month) plus additional efficiency credits tied to measured KV cache hit rate.
- Quant-enabled SKU (q4 variant) can receive a further 8–12% discount if AuroraScale agrees to a joint evaluation window and failure budget (fallback to fp16 in <5% of requests triggers rollback).

I've generated a short quant recommendation doc and a sample eval checklist (quant_recommendations.pdf - stub). Happy to run an A/B on a small slice of traffic.
